text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), which won a clear majority in Saturday's general election, nominated its leader Ivan Kostov as premier and former chairman of the UDF parliamentary group Yordan Sokolov as parliament speaker.
-- Marin Marinov, head of the Monetary Instruments department at the Bulgarian National Bank, was detained in connection with illegal financial deals, the Sofia prosecution said.
-- Bulgaria's April consumer price inflation is expected to slow to some five percent from 12.3 percent in March, said the National Statistics Institute.
-- Bulgaria's central bank cut the main interest rate to 6.2 percent monthly from 8.03 percent in line with the falling yield on short-term government securities, the BNB said.
-- The central bank said it had placed in receivership the private International Bank for Investment and Development due to a danger of insolvency.
-- President Petar Stoyanov is expected to issue a decree convening the new parliament for its first session on May 7, the date proposed to him by the likely premier, UDF leader Ivan Kostov.

-- Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev, who is likely to retain his post in the future UDF cabinet, said he opposed the proposal of the UDF leader Ivan Kostov that the secret police files of leading politicians and supreme court judges should be opened.

-- Bulgaria and Turkey are going to be allies in NATO very soon, said visiting Turkish Defence Minister Turhan Tayan after talks with his Bulgarian counterpart Georgi Ananiev. Tayan, who was on one-day working visit to Bulgaria, said that NATO expansion should begin with the Balkan countries.
-- The caretaker cabinet raised the salaries of state employees by 38 percent and the pensions five-fold from the beginning of May.

-- The newly-elected chairwoman of the UDF parliamentary group Ekaterina Mihailova said that the laws for introduction of a currency board regime and the state budget are to be the first to be passed by the new parliament within 30 days.
